newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia says MAS can raise fares.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia says MAS can raise fares.

text.p: The Malaysian government has given Malaysian Airline System Bhd (MAS) its approval to raise international air fares by between three and 10 percent, the national Bernama news agency said on Wednesday.
Bernama was quoting Transport Minister Ling Liong Sik after a weekly Cabinet meeting.
MAS had said in November it had submitted a proposal to the government for a fare hike of around three percent, citing rising jet fuel pices as the main reason.
MAS chairman Tajudin Ramli said that jet fuel prices account for around 10 percent of the airline's total operating cost.
The Malaysian government had earlier announced that it was agreeable to a price rise on international routes, as the government only controlled domestic fares.
About 65 percent of MAS's fuel is consumed by aircraft serving international flights.
The International Air Transport Association has recommended a rise in air fares worldwide due to the rise in fuel prices over several years.
On Monday, Singapore Airlines Ltd said it has raised international passenger air fares by three percent as of December 15, 1996, citing fuel prices.
